text: Retrieval augmented generation grounds a language model in external documents. A retriever fetches passages relevant to the question and the generator conditions its answer on them, which reduces hallucination and lets the system cite sources.

BM25 is a lexical ranking function that scores documents by term frequency and inverse document frequency with length normalisation. It is strong on exact keyword matches such as identifiers and rare technical terms.
Dense embedding models map text to vectors so that semantically similar passages lie close together. Nearest neighbour search over these vectors finds paraphrases that share no words with the query.
Reciprocal rank fusion merges several ranked lists by summing the inverse of each item's rank. It needs no score calibration, so it is a simple way to combine keyword and semantic search results.

Chunking splits long documents into smaller passages before indexing. Overlapping windows preserve context across boundaries, while chunks that are too large dilute the signal and chunks that are too small lose meaning.

Normalized discounted cumulative gain rewards placing relevant results near the top of a ranking. Each hit is discounted by the logarithm of its position and the total is divided by the best achievable ordering.
Mean reciprocal rank averages the inverse rank of the first relevant result across queries. It suits tasks where users only need one good answer and cares little about the rest of the list.

Recall at k measures the share of all relevant documents that appear in the top k results. High recall in the first stage matters because a later reranker cannot recover a document that was never retrieved.

A cross encoder reranker reads the query and a candidate passage together and outputs a relevance score. It is more accurate than a bi encoder but too slow to run over a whole corpus, so it reorders a short candidate list.

Prompt injection hides instructions inside retrieved content so that the model obeys the document instead of the user. Treat retrieved text as untrusted data and keep it separate from system instructions.
Faithfulness evaluation checks whether every claim in a generated answer is supported by the retrieved context. Unsupported claims are counted as hallucinations even when they happen to be true.

Approximate nearest neighbour indexes such as HNSW graphs trade a small loss in recall for large speedups on million scale vector collections. Index parameters control the balance between build time, memory and accuracy.
